title: Preparation of standard oxalic acid solution
objective: Calculate the mass of oxalic acid crystals needed for a solution of stated normality and volume
Weigh the mass accurately and transfer it completely into a volumetric flask
Make the solution up to the mark and mix thoroughly
Explain why oxalic acid is a suitable PRIMARY standard

theory.statement: Oxalic acid crystals, H2C2O4·2H2O, are stable, of precisely known formula, and non-hygroscopic — the properties needed for a primary standard, a substance whose solution's concentration can be known exactly from its weighed mass alone, with no titration required.
theory.derivationNote: Molarity = mass / (molar mass × volume in litre). Because oxalic acid is diacidic (it can donate two protons), its normality for acid-base purposes is twice its molarity: N = M × 2. A 250 mL flask of 0.1 N oxalic acid therefore needs mass = 0.1 × 63.04(equivalent mass) × 0.250 L ≈ 1.575 g of the dihydrate.
keyEquations: Normality N = M × basicity (= 2 for oxalic acid)

apparatus.name: Oxalic acid crystals (A.R.)
apparatus.why: The primary standard being weighed out

apparatus.name: Volumetric flask
apparatus.why: Made up to its precise, calibrated volume — never a beaker

apparatus.name: Funnel and wash bottle
apparatus.why: Ensures every trace of the weighed solid reaches the flask

variables.label: Made up exactly to the mark

procedure.text: Calculate the mass of oxalic acid crystals needed for the stated normality and flask volume.
Weigh out this mass accurately in a weighing bottle.
Transfer the solid into the volumetric flask through a funnel, rinsing the weighing bottle and funnel thoroughly with distilled water.
Dissolve completely by swirling, then add water up to just below the graduation mark.
Make up to the mark exactly, reading the meniscus at eye level, and mix by inverting several times.
Calculate the exact molarity and normality of the solution prepared.

steps: Molarity = mass / (molar mass × volume in L)

expectedResult.quantity: Normality of the standard oxalic acid solution prepared
expectedResult.statement: Weighing 1.575 g of oxalic acid dihydrate into a 250 mL volumetric flask and making up to the mark gives a solution of almost exactly 0.1 N — known precisely from the mass alone, with no titration needed.

safety: Oxalic acid is toxic if ingested and irritating to skin/eyes — wash hands after use.
Handle the volumetric flask carefully; a chipped graduation mark makes the volume unreliable.
sourcesOfError: Solid left in the weighing bottle or funnel lowers the true concentration below the calculated value.
Overshooting the graduation mark dilutes the solution.
A wet flask, if wrongly assumed dry, does not itself introduce an error since it is made up to volume, but wet weighing paper does.

viva.question: What properties make oxalic acid crystals suitable as a primary standard?
viva.expectedConcept: They are stable in air (not hygroscopic or efflorescent), of precisely known, constant composition, and available in high purity, so a weighed mass gives an exactly known number of moles.
viva.commonMisconception: Thinking any solid acid would serve equally well as a primary standard.

viva.question: Why must the solid be rinsed completely into the flask rather than just tipped in?
viva.expectedConcept: Any solid left in the weighing bottle or funnel is mass that was weighed but never dissolved, so the actual concentration would be lower than calculated from the weighed mass.
viva.answerLogic: Weighed mass must equal dissolved mass.
viva.commonMisconception: Assuming a quick tip-in is close enough.

viva.question: Why is a volumetric flask used instead of a beaker marked '250 mL'?
viva.expectedConcept: A volumetric flask is calibrated to contain its stated volume to a small, certified tolerance at its single graduation mark; a beaker's markings are only approximate and can be in error by several per cent.
viva.answerLogic: Calibration precision differs by orders of magnitude.
viva.commonMisconception: Treating any graduated glassware as equally accurate.

preLab.question: The equivalent mass of oxalic acid (H2C2O4·2H2O, molar mass 126) for acid-base reactions is:
preLab.feedback: Oxalic acid is diacidic (basicity 2), so equivalent mass = 126/2 = 63.
